sources.title: Checking object integrity for data uploads in Amazon S3
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 User Guide live documentation; page version not stated
sources.locator: Multipart uploads; checksum type matrix; full-object checksum conditions
sources.observed_operation: AWS multipart initiation, part upload, completion, checksum validation and retrieval
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Full-object multipart validation is available for CRC64NVME, CRC32 and CRC32C; SHA-256 is composite-only. Multipart ETag is not a whole-object MD5. When using checksum mode, part numbers must be consecutive from 1. For existing algorithms, a completion checksum header can be accepted but not validated or stored if the algorithm was omitted at initiation.
sources.applicability: AWS checksum behavior only; exact provider, operation, algorithm and checksum scope require confirmation.

sources.title: Uppy Golden Retriever documentation

sources.locator: IndexedDB, optional Service Worker storage, restore behavior
sources.observed_operation: Browser-side persistence and restoration of selected files and Uppy state
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: IndexedDB stores file data up to 10 MiB per file by default. Optional Service Worker storage can temporarily retain references to larger files, but these do not persist through browser crashes or restarts; failed restores can offer reselection.
sources.applicability: Browser recovery behavior, separate from storage-service part limits; pin and test deployed library.

sources.title: tus Resumable Upload Protocol 1.0.x
sources.locator: Upload-Length, HEAD, PATCH, Upload-Offset; checksum, expiration and termination extensions
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: HEAD reports the current offset and PATCH continues at that offset. Checksum, expiration and termination are optional extensions that a server must advertise. The checksum extension verifies each PATCH body, not the complete file by itself.
sources.applicability: Analogous resumability mechanism; does not define object-store compatibility or final archival verification.

sources.title: tusd v2.10.1 S3 storage backend
sources.locator: Storage format; temporary disk; consistency and locking; R2 part sizing
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: The backend stores metadata and multipart parts; the final object appears only after completion. PATCH bodies may use temporary disk. It requires strong read-after-write consistency; multiple instances sharing a bucket require distributed locking. R2 needs equal-sized nonfinal parts and the docs recommend 50 MiB part sizing in that R2 context.
sources.applicability: Version-specific server-route requirements; compatible API behavior and operations must be tested against the selected provider.

sources.title: Amazon S3 multipart upload overview
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 User Guide live documentation; page version not stated
sources.locator: ListParts; completion manifest; concurrent uploads; multipart pricing
sources.observed_operation: CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, ListParts, CompleteMultipartUpload and abort
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: ListParts returns at most 1,000 and must be paginated. AWS says to maintain the part-number/ETag list used for completion rather than using a listing as the completion payload. In-progress part storage is billed until complete or abort; lifecycle cleanup is recommended.
sources.applicability: AWS workflow only; reconcile and test provider-specific behavior.

sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: AWS documents final-write conditional behavior and 412/409 race responses. Conditions do not reserve an in-progress multipart upload at initiation or on UploadPart; a 409 on completion may require restarting the MPU.
sources.applicability: AWS-specific supplementary race control, not a replacement for application idempotency or archive-provider confirmation.
